title: NFL insider says there’s ‘a scenario’ where Rams don’t keep Puka Nacua
text:
NFL insider says there’s ‘a scenario’ where Rams don’t keep Puka Nacua Schedule NFL News Draft Fantasy Odds Betting Newsletter Shop RAMS NFL insider says there’s ‘a scenario’ where Rams don’t keep Puka Nacua
 Oliver G. Rams Wire Nov. 18, 2026, 8:20 a.m. PT Los Angeles Rams receiver Puka Nacua won't see the field for a while while he recovers from a knee injury, and one NFL insider sees a world in which 2026 is the young pass-catcher's final year with the team.
 ESPN’s Dan Graziano didn’t rule out the Rams letting Nacua walk in free agency after his tumultuous, although productive, fourth year in the NFL. Graziano wrote that he "could at least imagine a scenario in which the Rams let him hit free agency, or franchise him and listen to offers" because of his off-field issues and injury concerns.
 Because Nacua wasn't a first-round pick, the Rams didn't have a fifth-year option on his contract, and he'll be a free agent in 2027 unless he and the team agree to a contract extension before then. The franchise tag is also an option . Before his injury, Nacua had caught 70 passes for 715 yards and four touchdowns in seven games.
 The issues Graziano flagged that could give the Rams pause are Nacua's off-field issues and his health.
 Nacua, who was eligible for a new deal but didn't receive an extension in 2026, made headlines for his off-field behavior that included comments about officials and an antisemitic dance he did on a livestream in December. The league fined him $25,000 for questioning the integrity of its officials. Then, he was accused of biting a woman and making an antisemitic comment on New Year’s Eve, and eventually spent some time in rehab. Graziano noted he could still face league discipline under the personal conduct policy.

Nacua has only played a full 17-game season once in his four-year career, too — during his rookie season in 2023. He missed two games earlier this season with hip and groin injuries and has been on injured reserve since after Week 9 with a knee injury that will cost him at least a month.
 “He’s 25 years old and a brilliant player," Graziano write, "but his play style makes you wonder about his longevity,”
 NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reported earlier this year that a deal was unlikely before the regular season. He said talks would more likely heat up next offseason, because the Rams want to see improvement in Nacua’s personal behavior. Coach Sean McVay has said he hopes Nacua is a Ram “for a really long time.” Nacua also hired Win Sports Group before the season . The agency represents Smith-Njigba, now the highest-paid receiver in NFL history, and Zay Flowers, who just signed a $140 million extension with the Ravens.
 Before the season, Graziano predicted the Rams would give Nacua a four-year, $156 million extension with $90 million guaranteed. At $39 million per year, that would sit just below Ja’Marr Chase and ahead of Justin Jefferson.
 But given Nacua's injury history and the Rams' current roster configuration that includes new deals for Myles Garrett and Trent McDuffie (as well as impending negotiations for other Rams stars like Byron Young, Kobie Turner and Steve Avila), an extension for Nacua isn't necessarily guaranteed anymore.
 Not only would a new deal potentially be too expensive, but there could be a real market for Nacua if the Rams are ready to move on from the young and productive offensive weapon.
